summary: Updates the new Telnet specification from RFC 495 to include modifications suggested since it was published. It also declares a moratorium on further changes, because the changeover from old to new Telnet was only a few months away.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC lists revisions to the new Telnet documents and then pauses further changes until the planned transition. It allows work on additional options to continue.

subtitle: A final set of changes to the new Telnet specifications before the planned switchover.

tldr.problem: Suggestions for changes had accumulated while the scheduled transition from the old Telnet to the new version was approaching.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 562 lists revisions to the Telnet protocol and option documents, including clarifications and an End of Subnegotiation Parameters command.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 495 and calls for a moratorium on further specification changes until after the switchover, while allowing new options.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 562 as Unknown and records that it updates RFC 495. It is a change list for the revised Telnet documents.

sections.title: Why the Documents Were Revised
sections.content:
Almost four months had passed since publication of the new Telnet Protocol specification, and the planned switch from old Telnet to new Telnet was four months away. RFC 562 says it was time to incorporate the suggestions already made.

The attached revised protocol and option documents replace the earlier NIC documents.
sections.plainLanguage: The new Telnet documents had received a small number of suggested changes, and a transition date was getting close. The author proposes incorporating the changes and then holding the specification steady.

sections.title: Protocol Clarifications
sections.content:
The RFC lists changes by page of the earlier protocol document. These include removing the phrase blocked on input, expanding explanations of IP and AO, clarifying print position, revising the SYNCH description to align with RFC 529, and expanding the CR-NUL explanation.

It also defines the End of Subnegotiation Parameters command, SE.
sections.plainLanguage: Several changes explain existing Telnet behavior more clearly. Another adds a command to mark the end of option subnegotiation parameters.

sections.title: Option Rules and the Moratorium
sections.content:
The revised option specifications explain the use of SE and require that an IAC byte inside subnegotiation parameters be doubled.

RFC 562 declares a moratorium on incorporating additional suggestions until after the switchover. It explicitly says the moratorium does not prevent specifying additional options.
sections.plainLanguage: The option rules define how to end parameter data and how to represent an IAC byte within it. Other specification changes pause during the transition, but new options remain possible.
